Welcome! I was also part of the Reddit transition :). If I mas ask, and if I'm allowed to on this sub, whats it like being a nurse? I start freshman year of college next year and I am going to major in nursing. Any major tips or warnings?

We always need more nurses.
Nursing is pretty awesome. Except for the paperwork, and all the pills. Most of my work is in nursing home/long-term care. I enjoy nursing a lot, but I recognize that it isn't for everybody, and there are a lot of people in the field that should have done other things, but frankly we're rarely in a position where we can turn away help. =P
The things I enjoy most? Healing wounds. I love changing dressings, packing wounds, and watching them get better every few days. I've made holes in people bigger than my fist gradually disappear. Additionally, watching people get better and regain independence. Getting someone from bed-bound to walking out the door under their own power is an amazing thing, even if there are a lot of bumps along the way. You get to see a lot of life happen.
And death. There are good deaths and bad deaths; and sometimes the difference depends on you and your staff.
Also, people are dicks. People in pain are more so, and people who have a parent or spouse in pain are more so still. The reason the thank-yous feel so good is because they can be pretty rare.
My biggest tip AND warning is smells. Learn to ignore your nose. Even a good day can stink, and a bad day will get worse. Unhealthy people are going to smell bad, and I can't think of a single unhealthy lifestyle that doesn't lead to bad smells. A tip that helped me in clinical was practicing pouring meds. I can pour an accurate dose of over-the-counter meds by feel alone, and its because I'd drill myself on tylenol, fish oil, and fluoxetine (that was what my wife was on when I was in school). Having to fish a lone aspirin or Vitamin D out of a med cup full of narcotics and cardiac meds is a pain and the seconds you lose will gang up on you towards the end of your shift.
I'm actually going back for my RN this fall, which would be my last bit of advice. If you can do it, go right for your RN/BSN. I didn't, because I was working full time while schooling and most nursing schools that care about their graduation rates will tell you that you can't take the full course load and work a full time job. Nursing school is intense. If you have to work like I did, get a job as an LNA/CNA. This keeps you in a health care setting at work, gives you a boss that understands the rigors of what you're going through, and it typically pays a lot more than minimum wage. Can't spare the cash for LNA/CNA training? Don't worry; after your first semester in nursing school you're basically qualified for Licensure/Certification as a Nursing Aid.
